playArea.grid: Same grid as heightmap.png: pixel (col, row) is centered on heightmap vertex (col, row), i.e. x = (col - 800) * 5, z = (row - 800) * 5. Row 0 = -z (north), column 0 = -x (west). The image covers x, z in [-4002.5, 4002.5] m.
playArea.uv: u = (x + 4002.5) / 8005, v_down = (z + 4002.5) / 8005 (v_down = 0 at the top row). With a PlaneGeometry spanning the play area the error is at most half a texel.
playArea.values: linear_albedo = srgb_to_linear(value / 255). Mean = 0.25 (value 137). Grayscale: tint it in the shader. To use it as a multiplier on a base color, divide the decoded value by 0.25.
playArea.filled: 0.17% of pixels (no image data or grazing modelled light) are copied from the nearest real pixel.

source.dataset: Mars 2020 HiRISE orthorectified image mosaic, 25 cm/px (JEZ_hirise_soc_007_orthoMosaic_25cm_Ortho_blend120), area-averaged to 2.5 m then 5 m
source.citation: Fergason, R.L., Galuszka, D.M., Hare, T.M. (2020), High-Resolution Imaging Science Experiment Orthorectified Image Mosaic for Mars 2020 Surface Operations, U.S. Geological Survey data release, doi:10.5066/P9QJDP48. HiRISE: McEwen, A.S., et al. (2007), J. Geophys. Res. 112, E05S02
source.shadingDem: heightmap.png (USGS Mars 2020 TRN HiRISE 1 m DTM at 5 m), same grid

processing: Area-averaged from 25 cm to 2.5 m (cached) and resampled to the play-area grid (azimuthal equidistant, 5 m) by area averaging.

Shading removal: local Lambert fit I ~ g * (n . s) with n from heightmap.png, Gaussian-weighted least squares (sigma 400 m). Only the shading relative to flat ground is divided out, so real albedo differences (dark sand, light-toned rock) are kept. Fitted Sun elevation p10/p50/p90 = [33.5, 45.4, 68.0] deg, azimuth (from north toward east) [211.8, 261.8, 280.0] deg.
Scaled so the mean is linear albedo 0.25, clipped to 0.3..2.5 times the mean.
limits: Absolute albedo is not calibrated: the mosaic is stretched per image; only relative brightness is real.
Rocks, ripples and craters smaller than ~20 m keep the shading and shadows of the original afternoon Sun (from the west), because the 5 m heights cannot model them.
